In [[mathematics]], the '''symmetric closure''' of a [[binary relation]] <math>R</math> on a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] <math>X</math> is the smallest [[symmetric relation]] on <math>X</math> that contains <math>R.</math>

For example, if <math>X</math> is a set of airports and <math>xRy</math> means "there is a direct flight from airport <math>x</math> to airport <math>y</math>", then the symmetric closure of <math>R</math> is the relation "there is a direct flight either from <math>x</math> to <math>y</math> or from <math>y</math> to <math>x</math>". Or, if <math>X</math> is the set of humans and <math>R</math> is the relation 'parent of', then the symmetric closure of <math>R</math> is the relation "<math>x</math> is a parent or a child of <math>y</math>".

== Definition ==

The symmetric closure <math>S</math> of a relation <math>R</math> on a set <math>X</math> is given by
<math display=block>S = R \cup \{ (y, x) : (x, y) \in R \}.</math>

In other words, the symmetric closure of <math>R</math> is the union of <math>R</math> with its [[converse relation]], <math>R^{\operatorname{T}}.</math>
